answer: A stake-and-slash registry makes Sybil attacks costly: each agent address must lock a bond before its vote counts, and a signed proof of double-voting burns that bond. To gain k votes an attacker must post k independent bonds, so cost scales linearly with fake identities while the reward stays fixed. A public log is the lantern that exposes duplicate votes, a receipt thread ties every ballot back to its own locked bond, and a walnut posted as collateral makes each extra identity a real expense. Attacking pays only if the loot exceeds the total slashed stake.
